answer: The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 14 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. Because the kernel hash is checked against the opal checkpoint at intake, the lagoon audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs hence has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
